notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 6 of their last 7 games, including the last one. Nikita Kucherov takes shifts on two lines, L1 and L2. Emil Lilleberg is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Hedman and McDonagh.
Yanni Gourde is on the injured non-roster list (hip surgery) and has not played this season. Ilya Mikheyev has taken his spot beside Zemgus Girgensons and Pontus Holmberg.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 41% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 28 seconds at a time, against 67 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (9 of 16 changes).

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 8 games, including the last one. Nazem Kadri takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L4. Noah Juulsen is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Manson and Malinski.
T.J. Hughes is day to day, reported after he played in their last game.
Gavin Brindley was added to the roster on Oct 15 and has played beside Parker Kelly and Fedor Svechkov.

COL.head: The Avalanche start a half-step ahead
COL.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Lightning can still swing it if they keep the shots coming.

TBL.head: Close, but the Avalanche have the slight edge
TBL.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Lightning’s best way to tip it is piling up shots.

story.head: Best against best
paras: The Lightning come in at 5-2-0, the Avalanche at 5-2-1. Two of the league’s best teams meet.

It’s strength against strength: the Avalanche are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Lightning are one of the best at keeping shots away. At home, Jared Bednar likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Bolts’ first line.
